prompt: NFL field markings: how wide is the painted goal line?
teach: Other field lines are 4 inches wide; the goal line is double that.

prompt: Inflation range for an official NFL game ball?
teach: The Referee is the sole judge of whether game balls meet the specs.

source.ref: NFL Rule 2, Section 1 — The Ball, Dimensions

prompt: NFL offense at the snap: fewest players it must have on the line of scrimmage?
teach: Eligible receivers must be on both ends of the line; those between them are ineligible.

source.ref: NFL Rule 7, Section 5, Article 1 — Offensive Team

prompt: NFL punt returner gives an invalid fair-catch signal. Penalty?
teach: It's marked off from where he signaled, not where the play ended.

source.ref: NFL Rule 10, Section 2 — Invalid Fair Catch Signal

prompt: NFL try: the play ends in what would normally be a safety by the defense. Offense scores?
teach: A defensive touchdown during a try, like a blocked-kick return, is worth 2.

source.ref: NFL Rule 11, Section 3, Article 2 — Results of a Try

prompt: NFL runner fumbles forward out of the opponent's end zone. The call?
teach: Fumbling out of your own end zone, if you sent it there, is a safety instead.

source.ref: NFL Rule 8, Section 7 — Fumble out of bounds in end zone

prompt: Untouched missed NFL field goal, kicked from beyond the 20. Defense takes over where?
teach: If the kick came from inside the 20, they get it at the 20 instead.

source.ref: NFL Rule 11, Section 4, Article 2 — Missed Field Goals

prompt: NFL player is flagged for taunting twice in the same game. Result?
teach: It applies even if the penalty is declined, and pregame-warmup fouls carry over.

source.ref: NFL Rule 12, Section 4, Article 1 — Automatic Disqualification

prompt: How long is an NFL postseason overtime period?
teach: Both teams must get the opportunity to possess the ball in it.

source.ref: NFL Rule 16, Section 1, Article 4 — Overtime in Postseason

prompt: NFL: minimum break between the 1st and 2nd quarters?
teach: Only the head coach, not an assistant, may enter then to check an injured player.

prompt: NFL penalty for an offensive chop block?
teach: It's a high-low double team: one blocker hits the thigh or below while another goes high.

source.ref: NFL Rule 12, Section 2, Article 5 — Chop Block

prompt: NFL, after the 2-minute warning: a teammate recovers a 2nd-down fumble 5 yards ahead. Next snap?
teach: Only the fumbler may recover and advance it, the same as on 4th down and tries.

source.ref: NFL Rule 8, Section 7, Article 6 — Fumble After Two-Minute Warning

prompt: NFL yard-line numbers: how far in from the sideline do their bottoms start?
teach: Each white numeral measures 2 yards tall.

source.ref: NFL Rule 1 — Additional Field Markings, Field Numerals

prompt: Minimum width of the solid white border around an NFL field?
teach: Borders 12 feet or wider don't need the extra broken yellow line outside them.

prompt: Inside diameter of an NBA rim?
teach: The white cord net hanging from it is also 18 inches long.

prompt: NBA: gap from the backboard face to the nearest inside edge of the rim?
teach: The ring must be painted orange.

prompt: Air pressure range for an official NBA game ball?
teach: Each team must get at least nine balls for pregame warmups.

prompt: NBA sideline hash marks for advanced throw-ins sit how far from the baseline?
teach: Late-game timeouts let a team inbound there in its frontcourt.

source.ref: NBA Rule 1, Section I; Rule 5, Section VI

prompt: NBA player picks up his 6th foul, but every sub has already fouled out. Result?
teach: His team is charged a technical foul, and again for each later foul he commits.

prompt: NBA: seconds a shooter has to attempt a free throw once he controls the ball?
teach: He can't cross the line's plane until the ball touches the ring or backboard.

source.ref: NBA Rule 9, Section I — Positions and Violations

prompt: NBA shot clock starts showing tenths of a second at what reading?
teach: The game clock shows tenths only in the last minute of each period.

prompt: NBA, 1st through 3rd quarters: a made basket stops the clock during the final what?
teach: In the 4th quarter and overtime it stops after makes in the last 2 minutes.

source.ref: NBA Rule 5, Section V — Stoppage of Timing Devices

prompt: NBA player accidentally scores in his own basket. Who's credited?
teach: Shooting at the wrong basket on purpose is a violation instead.

prompt: NBA team commits its 2nd delay-of-game violation of the game. The call?
teach: The first is a warning; checking in with an untucked jersey can count as one.

prompt: NBA defensive 3-second violation. The penalty?
teach: The shot clock stays the same or resets to 14, whichever is greater.

source.ref: NBA Rule 10, Section VII — Defensive Three-Second Rule

prompt: NBA: max seconds a player below the FT line extended may dribble with his back to the basket?
teach: Picking up the ball or a defensive deflection ends the count.

source.ref: NBA Rule 10, Section XVI — Five-Second Back-to-the-Basket

prompt: NBA overtime, first 3 minutes: penalty free throws start on which team foul?
teach: A team under that quota may commit one foul without penalty in the last 2 minutes.

source.ref: NBA Rule 12B, Section V — Free Throw Penalty Situations

prompt: MLB: distance from home plate to second base?
teach: First to third base is the same distance across the diamond.

source.ref: MLB Rule 2.01 — Layout of the Field

prompt: MLB parks built after June 1, 1958: minimum distance down each foul line?
teach: Those parks also need at least 400 feet to center field.

prompt: MLB mound: slope from 6 inches in front of the rubber toward home?
teach: It runs 6 feet toward the plate and must be uniform.

source.ref: MLB Rule 2.01 — Layout of the Field

prompt: MLB: deepest cup (indentation) allowed in the end of a bat?
teach: The cup must be 1 to 2 inches across and curved, with nothing added.

prompt: Max length of an MLB first baseman's mitt, top to bottom?
teach: It can be no more than 8 inches wide across the palm.

prompt: Max circumference of an MLB catcher's mitt?
teach: It can't be more than 15½ inches from top to bottom either.

prompt: MLB: batting out of order is appealed after the improper batter singles. Who's out?
teach: Any advance or run made because of the improper batter's hit is wiped out.

source.ref: MLB Rule 6.03(b) — Batting Out of Turn

prompt: Still holding his bat, an MLB batter-runner hits his own fair ball again in fair ground. Call?
teach: If a dropped bat rolls into the ball with no intent, the ball stays alive.

prompt: A declared infield fly hits a runner while he's touching his base. MLB call?
teach: Off the base, that same runner would be out along with the batter.

prompt: MLB third-base coach grabs the runner and helps him back to the bag. The call?
teach: Leaving the box to draw a throw with a man on 3rd is also interference.

prompt: Fair grounder hits an MLB umpire before passing any infielder. Batter gets?
teach: Once it has passed an infielder other than the pitcher, it stays in play.

prompt: MLB starting pitcher is also his team's DH, then gets pulled from the mound. Can he keep batting?
teach: He's listed twice on a 10-name lineup card, but can't pitch again that game.

source.ref: MLB Rule 5.11(b) — Starting Pitcher as Designated Hitter

prompt: MLB pitcher quick-pitches the batter with the bases empty. The call?
teach: With runners on base, a quick pitch is a balk instead.

prompt: NFL: how many officials work a game?
teach: Referee, Umpire, Down Judge, Line Judge, Field Judge, Side Judge and Back Judge.

source.ref: NFL Rule 19, Section 1, Article 1 — Game Officials

prompt: NFL: can a 10-second runoff ever be charged against the defense?
teach: The timing rules say a runoff can never be assessed against the defensive team.

source.ref: NFL Rule 4, Section 5, Article 4, Note 9 — Injury Timeouts after Two-Minute Warning

prompt: NFL: minimum tip diameter of a conical cleat?
teach: Cleats made of metal or anything that may chip or fracture are banned.

source.ref: NFL Rule 5, Section 4, Article 4, Item 4 — Improper Cleats

prompt: NFL: after a safety, the free kick comes from which yard line?
teach: The safety kick may be a punt, drop kick or place kick, and a tee may be used.

source.ref: NFL Rule 11, Section 5, Article 2 — Ball in Play after Safety

prompt: NBA: how long is the substitution box in front of the scorer's table?
teach: Its hash marks sit 4 feet on each side of the midcourt line.

prompt: NBA: fewest balls each team must get for pregame warmups?
teach: The game ball must be inflated to between 7½ and 8½ pounds of pressure.

prompt: NBA backboard: width of the white rectangle behind the rim?
teach: Its 2-inch lines frame a box 18 inches tall.

prompt: NBA: how long is the net hanging from the rim?
teach: The cord must be 30 to 120 thread, built to check the ball momentarily.

prompt: How many strikes for a strikeout?
teach: A foul tip caught with two strikes also counts as strike three.

prompt: Outs per team in each half-inning?
teach: When three offensive players are legally put out, that team takes the field.

source.ref: Official Baseball Rules 5.09(e) — Retiring the Side

prompt: Players per team in the field on defense?
teach: Rule 1.01: baseball is a game between two teams of nine players each.

prompt: A pitch outside the zone hits a batter who tried to avoid it. The call?
teach: If he makes no try to avoid it, it's only a ball; in the zone, it's a strike.

source.ref: Official Baseball Rules 5.05(b)(2) — Hit by pitch

prompt: Batter fouls off the first pitch. The call?
teach: Fouls count as strikes until two; after that the count holds, except on a bunt.

source.ref: Official Baseball Rules — Definitions of Terms (Strike)

prompt: MLB infield: stated radius of the grass line at the outer edge of the dirt?
teach: The permitted average measurement is more than 94 feet and less than 96 feet.

prompt: MLB field: recommended minimum clearance from home plate or a base line to an obstruction?
teach: For fields built after June 1, 1958, each foul line must extend at least 325 feet.

prompt: MLB home plate: length of either adjacent side?
teach: The edge facing the pitcher is 17 inches long.

prompt: NFL field markings: width and length of each inbounds hash mark?
teach: The rulebook separately describes the college marks as 12 inches long.

prompt: NFL Try: points for a defensive touchdown?
teach: A Try is one untimed scrimmage down after a touchdown.

prompt: NBA lane: size of each lane-space mark?
teach: The lane boundary lines are part of the lane, but the lane-space and neutral-zone marks are not.

prompt: NBA defensive three-second violation with 10 seconds on the shot clock: reset to what?
teach: The offense also gets a new 8-second count to advance the ball from the backcourt.

prompt: NBA delay of game: result of the first offense?
teach: Each successive delay-of-game offense is assessed a team technical foul.

prompt: MLB infield positioning: minimum infielders with both feet on each side of second base?
teach: The two infielders on each side cannot switch sides during that inning.

prompt: MLB strike zone: where is the upper boundary for a batter in a normal stance?
teach: The lower boundary is the hollow beneath the kneecap.

prompt: MLB strike zone: where is the lower boundary for a batter in a normal stance?
teach: The upper boundary is the midpoint between the shoulders and uniform pants.

prompt: MLB: how many base coaches may the batting team provide?
teach: The coaches must stay in their boxes while the pitcher is on the plate.

prompt: MLB manager signals an intentional walk. What does the umpire award?
teach: The rule treats the award as if the batter received four pitches outside the zone.

prompt: MLB: may a player who has been removed from a game re-enter?
teach: The umpire-in-chief must direct an improperly re-entering player to leave.

prompt: MLB runner returning to first overruns it with both feet in foul ground. Before advancing, what must he do?
teach: A runner may not take a flying start from behind his base.

prompt: MLB: a batter forces a runner forward onto a base occupied by a runner ahead. Who is entitled to that base?
teach: When both runners are touching the base, the preceding runner is out when tagged.

prompt: MLB time play: a runner touches home before a non-force third out. Does the run score?
teach: A batter-runner's third out before first base also cancels the run.

prompt: MLB runner deliberately runs the bases in reverse order to confuse the defense. Ruling?
teach: Running in reverse order to confuse the defense is an out.

prompt: MLB runner leaves a base before a fly ball is caught. What must he do to avoid an appeal out?
teach: The rule defines retouching as tagging up and starting from contact with the base after the catch.

prompt: MLB catcher is hindered by batter interference and no runner is put out. Who is out?
teach: The runner attempting to score is returned to the base he last occupied.

prompt: MLB: may a runner return to touch a missed base after a following runner scores?
wrong: Only if the ball is dead
teach: The defense may still appeal the missed base when a runner cannot return to correct it.

prompt: MLB: minimum infielders besides the pitcher and catcher with both feet in front of the dirt boundary?
teach: At least two of those infielders must be positioned on each side of second base.

prompt: MLB batter refuses to take his position in the box. What does the umpire call?
teach: The ball is dead and runners may not advance on this strike.

prompt: NFL touchdown: what must cross the opponent's goal line while the player has legal possession?
teach: The ball must be carried by an inbounds player and the play cannot be a touchback.

prompt: NFL: maximum legal forward passes by the offense during one down?
teach: A legal forward pass must be thrown from behind the line of scrimmage.

prompt: NFL runner goes out of bounds early in the second quarter. When does the game clock restart?
teach: After a change of possession, the clock instead starts on the snap.

prompt: NFL runner goes out of bounds during the final five minutes of the second half. Clock restarts when?
teach: Outside the final five minutes of the second half, the clock normally restarts on the referee's signal.

prompt: NFL incomplete forward pass: what happens to the game clock?
teach: The clock also stops when the ball goes out of bounds.

prompt: NFL fair-catch kick down: when does the game clock start?
teach: A fair-catch kick is an opportunity to score a field goal after a fair catch.

prompt: NFL replay reverses a ruling after the two-minute warning and makes the clock restart. What runoff applies?
teach: If fewer than 10 seconds remain after the runoff, the half or game ends.

prompt: NFL review triggers a 10-second runoff. How can either team avoid the runoff?
teach: If a timeout avoids the runoff, the game clock starts on the snap.

prompt: NFL successful field goal: maximum time that can run off the game clock during the attempt?
teach: The same five-second maximum applies to an unsuccessful kick that does not land in the field of play.

prompt: NFL try after a touchdown: is the down timed?
teach: A Try is one scrimmage down to add one or two points.

prompt: NFL ball dead behind defense's goal line from opponent's impetus, not a score or incomplete pass: result?
teach: A touchback is determined by the ball's status and which team supplied the impetus.

prompt: NFL Try results in a touchback. Is the Try successful?
teach: The Try ends when either team scores or the ball becomes dead by rule.

prompt: NFL touchdown on the final play of a period: is a Try normally still attempted?
teach: The rule has exceptions for sudden-death overtime and a fourth-period score when a Try cannot affect the outcome.

prompt: NFL offense bats a loose ball in the field of play toward the opponent's goal line. Penalty?
teach: The ban also covers batting a grounded loose ball in either end zone.

prompt: NBA: points for a successful field goal from outside the three-point line?
teach: A field goal from on or inside the arc counts two points.

prompt: NBA: points for a successful field goal on or inside the three-point line?
teach: A successful shot from outside the line counts three points.

prompt: NBA: how many points does a successful free throw count?
teach: A missed free throw tapped into the basket by a player counts two points.

prompt: NBA throw-in: when does the shot clock start?
teach: After a jump ball or missed free throw, it starts when a team obtains possession.

prompt: NBA shot-clock attempt: what must the ball contact after leaving the shooter's hand?
teach: The ball must leave the player's hand before the shot clock expires.

prompt: NBA frontcourt defensive kick violation with 13 seconds on the shot clock: reset to what?
teach: The shot clock is not reset to 24 seconds for this frontcourt violation.

prompt: NBA shot is in flight when the horn sounds; a defender touches it and it goes in. Does the basket count?
teach: If an offensive player touches the shot after the horn, the period has ended.

prompt: NBA: how many free throws are awarded for one technical foul?
teach: No free throws are awarded when opposing teams receive a double technical.

prompt: NBA opposing players receive double technical fouls during the same dead ball. How many free throws?
teach: A single technical foul, unlike a double technical, awards one free throw.

prompt: NBA ball is live with one team having six players on court. What is assessed?
teach: If that team had possession when discovered, it also loses possession.

prompt: NBA offensive player commits a personal foul during a throw-in before the ball is released. Call?
teach: The throw-in foul is an offensive foul whether or not the ball has been released.

prompt: NBA dribbler commits a charge; what happens to the ball?
teach: An offensive foul does not count as a team foul.

prompt: NBA game clock: when are tenths of a second displayed?
teach: The shot clock shows tenths when it reaches 4.9 seconds.

prompt: NBA technical foul follows a personal foul on the same team. Which free throw is attempted first?
teach: A technical foul carries one free-throw attempt.

prompt: NBA 4th quarter or OT: the clock stops after made baskets in the final how many minutes?
teach: In the first three periods, the made-basket stoppage applies during the final minute.

prompt: NBA missed free throw remains live; defender violates the lane. What does the shooter receive?
teach: If play would stop, a violation normally brings no penalty unless an opponent commits disconcertion.

prompt: MLB runner moves more than three feet from his basepath to avoid a tag. Ruling?
teach: A runner's basepath runs straight to the base he was trying to reach when the tag began.
